findings.title: Interpolation makes `isQueryWithRangeVariable` guard ineffective
findings.body: `runSplitQuery` now maps targets through `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` before `partition(queries, (query) => !querySupportsSplitting(query))`. `querySupportsSplitting` calls `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to avoid splitting queries containing `$__range` (or similar range variables), but after interpolation those variables have already been replaced with duration literals, so the guard no longer detects them. Queries that were deliberately excluded from time-splitting will now be split, and each subrequest will use an expression interpolated against the full request range rather than the intended unsplit query. This can produce incorrect result semantics. The check should be done against the pre-interpolation expression, or the guard must be intentionally re-evaluated with tests.

findings.title: Shard splitting applies template variables twice
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` now applies `applyTemplateVariables` to every target at line 52. Later, `splitQueriesByStreamShard` passes those same targets to `runSplitQuery` (line 163), and the modified `runSplitQuery` applies `applyTemplateVariables` again to its targets (querySplitting.ts line 299). This double interpolation is not guaranteed to be idempotent; in particular, if `request.filters` contains ad hoc filters, `applyTemplateVariables` can insert those filters into the expression on each call, duplicating filter selectors in the final query. The new test expectation that `applyTemplateVariables` is called five times for one target reflects this duplication rather than guarding against it. `runSplitQuery` should support skipping interpolation when the caller has already interpolated, or this path should avoid pre-interpolating before delegating.
